issues.description: Basic usage example uses next() on pipeline.nodes by name but ignores the name
issues.detail: The snippet uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to fetch the training node, which just returns the first node and ignores `name="train_model_node"`. For a literate doc, this is misleading: a reader copying it loses the invariant 'this is the train_model_node'. Use `pipeline.node("train_model_node")` or `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == "train_model_node")`.

issues.description: ImagePreview example has unreachable code after the first return
issues.detail: Inside `preview_correlation_matrix`, the URL `return` is followed by a commented data-URI alternative presented as an 'Or' option. A careful reader sees dead code under a single function. Split into two clearly named functions (`preview_correlation_matrix_url`, `preview_correlation_matrix_inline`) so each example is self-contained and runnable as written.

issues.description: make_preview_fn closure captures a mutable list without stating the invariant
issues.detail: The closure example captures `sample_data` by reference. If the caller mutates `sample_data` after node construction, the preview silently changes. The doc claims this is how to 'capture context' but does not state the invariant (snapshot at construction time vs live reference). Either copy inside the factory (`content=list(data_sample)`) or document the aliasing behavior explicitly.
issues.lines: using preview functions with data context

issues.detail: JSON-ish examples show `{"data": [...], "layout": {...}}` for Plotly and `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` for CustomPreview with literal ellipses. A reader cannot tell whether these are required schemas, suggestions, or placeholders. Either link to the contract definition (`preview_contract`) or replace ellipses with minimal concrete values so each block runs.

issues.description: Bare `node(...)` calls outside any Pipeline obscure how preview_fn is actually wired
issues.detail: Several later examples show `node(func=..., preview_fn=...)` as a top-level statement with no surrounding `Pipeline([...])` and no assignment. The first example established the pipeline pattern; the later snippets quietly drop it. For a literate doc, either consistently wrap in `Pipeline([...])` or assign to a variable so the reader sees the full lifecycle: build node, attach preview, call `.preview()`.

issues.description: Experimental warning lacks the invariant of what is stable vs. unstable
issues.detail: The warning says 'may change or be removed' but does not state which surface is experimental: the `preview_fn` kwarg on node, the `preview_contract` module, `node.preview()`, or all three. A user adopting this needs to know the blast radius of a breaking change. One sentence enumerating the experimental surface area would suffice.

review.summary: This is a documentation-only PR introducing a new "preview functions on nodes" section plus two style-config additions. As literate exposition it is mostly competent: each preview type gets a runnable example, and a closing best-practices list. UNDER-AUDITED on a few specifics — the basic-usage snippet retrieves a node by iteration instead of by name, the ImagePreview example has dead code after the first return, the closure example does not state its aliasing invariant, and several later examples drop the surrounding Pipeline scaffolding that the first example established. None of these are correctness bugs in shipped code, but they are exactly the kind of "the reader will copy this and be confused" issues a literate doc should not ship with. Tighten the six items above and this becomes RIGOROUS doc.
